title: Standard elements are stable under base change
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a ring map of finite presentation, $R\to R'$ any ring map, and $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ (of finite presentation over $R'$). If $a\in A$ is elementary standard, resp. strictly standard, in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element], then $a\otimes1$ is elementary standard, resp. strictly standard, in $A'$ over $R'$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CC (lemma-strictly-standard-base-change, line 295), Section 07C4

proof.text: Setup and the base-changed presentation. Assume $a$ is elementary standard, resp. strictly standard, in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]: there are a presentation, i.e. a surjective $R$-algebra map $\pi:P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to A$ with kernel $I=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and $0\le c\le\min(n,m)$ with (i) $a=a'\pi(\Delta)$, $\Delta=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}$, for some $a'\in A$, resp. $a=\sum_{|J|=c}a_J\pi(\Delta_J)$, $\Delta_J=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j=1,\dots,c,\,i\in J}$ ($J\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$), for some $a_J\in A$; and (ii) $p f_{c+j}\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)+I^2$ for $j=1,\dots,m-c$, where $p\in P$ is a lift of $a$. Let $\kappa:P\to P'=R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the coefficient map and $f'_j=\kappa(f_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] the $R'$-algebra map $\pi':P'\to A'=A\otimes_RR'$, $x_i\mapsto\pi(x_i)\otimes1$, is surjective with kernel $I'=(f'_1,\dots,f'_m)$: a presentation of $A'$ over $R'$ with the same $n$ and $m$, so the same $c$ satisfies $0\le c\le\min(n,m)$. Also $R'\to A'$ is of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition], so the notions of [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] apply to $a\otimes1\in A'$.

source.place: Lemma 07CC (lemma-strictly-standard-base-change, line 295) and its proof; Definition 07C7 (definition-strictly-standard, line 192)

proof.text: Compatibility of the two presentations. Let $\beta:A\to A'$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, a ring homomorphism. Then $\pi'\circ\kappa=\beta\circ\pi$ as maps $P\to A'$: both are $R$-algebra homomorphisms ($A'$ an $R$-algebra via $R\to R'\to A'$, which equals $r\mapsto r\otimes1=1\otimes r$; $\kappa$ is $R$-linear for the $R$-structure of $P'$ through $R\to R'$) and both send $x_i$ to $\pi(x_i)\otimes1$, so they are equal by the uniqueness clause of the universal property of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Consequently, if $p\in P$ lifts $a$ (i.e. $\pi(p)=a$), then $\kappa(p)$ lifts $a\otimes1$ (i.e. $\pi'(\kappa(p))=a\otimes1$), and for every $g\in P$ the image of $\kappa(g)$ in $A'$ is $\beta$ of the image of $g$ in $A$. Moreover $\kappa(I)\subseteq I'$ and $\kappa((f_1,\dots,f_c))\subseteq(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)$, since $\kappa$ is a ring homomorphism with $\kappa(f_j)=f'_j$.

source.place: Lemma 07CC (lemma-strictly-standard-base-change, line 295) and its proof; Definition 07C7 (definition-strictly-standard, line 192)

proof.text: Jacobian minors base change. By [lem-weil-pbc-partial-derivative-coefficient-map], $\partial f'_j/\partial x_i=\kappa(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)$ for all $i,j$. A determinant is a polynomial with integer coefficients in the entries (Leibniz formula $\det(M)=\sum_{\sigma}\mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_kM_{k\sigma(k)}$), so the ring homomorphism $\kappa$ commutes with it: $\Delta'=\det(\partial f'_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}=\kappa(\Delta)$ and $\Delta'_J=\det(\partial f'_j/\partial x_i)_{j=1,\dots,c,\,i\in J}=\kappa(\Delta_J)$ for every $J\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $|J|=c$. By step 2 their images in $A'$ are $\pi'(\Delta')=\beta(\pi(\Delta))$ and $\pi'(\Delta'_J)=\beta(\pi(\Delta_J))$.

source.place: Lemma 07CC (lemma-strictly-standard-base-change, line 295) and its proof; Definition 07C7 (definition-strictly-standard, line 192)

proof.text: The first condition. Apply the ring homomorphism $\beta$ to the identity (i) in $A$ and use step 3: in the elementary case $a\otimes1=\beta(a')\beta(\pi(\Delta))=(a'\otimes1)\,\pi'(\Delta')$; in the strictly standard case $a\otimes1=\sum_{|J|=c}(a_J\otimes1)\,\pi'(\Delta'_J)$. This is the first condition of [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] for $a\otimes1$ with respect to the presentation $\pi'$ of step 1, with $a'\otimes1$, resp. $a_J\otimes1$, as coefficients.

source.place: Lemma 07CC (lemma-strictly-standard-base-change, line 295) and its proof; Definition 07C7 (definition-strictly-standard, line 192)

proof.text: The second condition, and conclusion. By (ii) write $p f_{c+j}=\sum_{k=1}^cg_kf_k+\sum_{k,l=1}^mh_{kl}f_kf_l$ with $g_k,h_{kl}\in P$. Applying the ring homomorphism $\kappa$ gives $\kappa(p)f'_{c+j}=\sum_{k=1}^c\kappa(g_k)f'_k+\sum_{k,l}\kappa(h_{kl})f'_kf'_l\in(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)+(f'_1,\dots,f'_m)^2$ for $j=1,\dots,m-c$, and $\kappa(p)$ is a lift of $a\otimes1$ by step 2 (by [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] the condition does not depend on the lift). With the presentation $\pi'$ and the same $c$ (step 1) and step 4, $a\otimes1$ is elementary standard, resp. strictly standard, in $A'$ over $R'$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element].
